newsitem.title: UK: Dollar strong versus the yen, Euro bourses mixed.
newsitem.headline: Dollar strong versus the yen, Euro bourses mixed.

text.p: The dollar hit a 42-month high above 114 yen against the generally weak Japanese currency on Monday but failed to gain ground against the mark.

Key bourses put on a mixed showing by mid-afternoon. A surprise takeover bid helped the London stock market, Europe's busiest, attempt to get back nearer to recent record levels in the morning but investors' enthusiasm later waned.
The Frankfurt bourse advanced by one percent, boosted by a stream of encouraging corporate news, but Paris slipped back after a more positive start.
In early trading in New York, Wall Street stocks followed through on Friday's gains, with the Dow Jones industrial average adding around 25 points to 6,032 after gaining 14.54 on Friday.

Traders said a busy week for U.S. data could prompt caution on markets generally, given a common focus on the health of the American economy. The run of statistics will culminate in U.S. October jobs figures on Friday.

The yen suffered as Japanese investors kept on searching for higher-yielding investments abroad and amid uncertainty over the eventual political outcome after Japan's general election on October 20 left a hung parliament, market analysts said.
"Japanese investors are still showing a tremendous appetite for overseas assets," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London.
Compared with its advance against the yen, the dollar did little against the mark amid fading hopes for German rate cuts.

Elsewhere, the pound scaled a 16-month peak of $1.6145, hit 2.4590 marks, its strongest against the German currency since December 1995, and touched 184.35 yen, its highest against the yen since February 1993.
But a wave of speculative selling sent the South African rand to fresh lows of 4.6430 bid against the dollar and 7.4778 bid against the pound.
Heavyweight blue chip companies including Daimler-Benz, BASF and Volkswagen led an advance which added more than one percent to the 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt.

Shares in Volkswagen rose nearly three percent after the government proposed repealing laws governing the car giant which analysts said would give the group more freedom and small shareholders more influence.

The London stock market reversed slight opening losses to head higher after a boost from a surprise takeover bid for Northern Electric, later rejected by the utility. Northern Electric shares were up 120 pence at 650 pence, compared with the bid price of 630.
"We saw the bid lift the market," said one trader. "The market was going to be dull and drifting ahead of economic news this week but this has certainly lifted sentiment."

While London markets look ahead to the government budget in a month's time, this week's main economic diary entry in Britain is Wednesday's monthly monetary meeting between the finance minister and the governor of the Bank of England, although analysts expect no change in interest rates.
French shares weakened in modest volume, consolidating last week's gains ahead of U.S. data and next week's U.S. elections.
Lagardere fell around five percent to 157.10 francs, after a good run in previous weeks, on growing unease about its planned takeover of Thomson.

Meanwhile, for those looking for advice, market guru Elaine Garzarelli, best known for forecasting the October 1987 Wall Street crash, repeated a prediction that the U.S. market could drop between 15 percent and 25 percent by the end of this year.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5208 marks and 114.12 yen, compared with 1.5201 and 113.28 in late European business on Friday. It earlier hit a high of 114.40 yen.
STOCKS AT 1515 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 5.6 points at 4,028.0.
Germany's DAX index ended bourse floor trade 29.61 ahead at 2,703.83.
In Paris the CAC-40 index was down 11.29 at 2,151.14.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1515 GMT
Gold was fixed at $382.90 an ounce in the afternoon versus a morning setting of $382.80 and Friday's London close of $382.65. Silver edged up one cent to $4.93.
